::: {#def-causal-model .theorem}
## Causal model

A causal model $\mathcal C$ of an "observational" [NPSEM](#def-npsem) $\mathcal M$ under intervention regime $\Gamma$ combines $\mathcal M$ with its [interventional NPSEM](#def-interventional-npsem) $\mathcal M^{(\Gamma)}$, constraining the error term of each variable in $\mathcal M^{(\Gamma)}$ to equal the error term of the same variable in $\mathcal M$.

$$
\mathcal{C} = \mathcal{M} \cup \mathcal M^{(\Gamma)} \qquad \text{for all } V \in \mathbf V, \quad U_V = U^{(\Gamma)}_V
$$

The counterfactuals are the variables of $\mathcal M^{(\Gamma)}$: they are computed by recursive substitution through the same structural equations and the same error terms as the observed variables. A causal model is a structure, not yet a causal claim; what turns it into an [FFRCISTG](#def-ffrcistg) is the further assumptions that model makes.
:::
